text:
zoe: quick note from onboarding: teams using OIDC-to-token sidecars keep hitting issues because SDKs don't expose a pluggable credential provider. when sidecar rotates token, apps still use old token until restart.

vik: can you paste a short repro?

zoe: sure. typical setup: kube sidecar writes token to `/var/run/redwood/token`. app reads at startup (env points to path). sidecar does atomic swap on rotate. app still uses old token; restart required.

marco: we've seen that. current SDKs only support env var + default file path and read-once at init in some languages.

ashley: proposal: add a simple credential-provider interface to SDKs (get_token()) and a helper that watches a file or calls a refresh callback. default: read-once for short-lived CLI, but services can opt-in to `CredentialProvider.file(path, watch=true)` or `CredentialProvider.poll(path, interval_ms)`.

zoe: love that. makes it pluggable for sidecars (and also works with Vault/Seal/SSO hooks).

vik: parity note: node/go already have plug points, python does not. can we standardize the interface and ship minimal adapters for file/watch and env?

marco: also need a pattern for CI: ephemeral OIDC tokens in CI have TTL ~10m. CI builds should prefer `rw auth fetch --once --output ~/.config/redwood/token` at job start and fail if token close to expiry. SDKs could surface token-expires-soon warnings via telemetry.

infra-bot: created issue RBW-5122 (labels: devex,sdk,auth,ci).

ashley: also UX: add `rw auth provider add` command to register a provider in `~/.config/redwood/providers.json` with type=file|oidc|exec, path or exec-cmd. SDKs can read providers file and try providers in order. that avoids env var collisions and centralizes.

vik: security check: provider file should be user-readable only and documented. also require explicit opt-in for exec providers in CI (risk of leaking creds).

zoe: implement plan: 1) define interface doc (get_token(), token_expiry(), on_refresh(callback)). 2) python: add provider abstraction and file-watch adapter. 3) node/go: expose same interface and ship provider adapters. 4) CLI: `rw auth provider` helpers + `rw auth status` shows active provider. 5) add telemetry event `auth.provider.refresh` and `auth.provider.fallback` for observability.

marco: tests: simulate sidecar atomic swap + provider file-watch, simulate OIDC exec refreshing token, simulate CI ephemeral fetch and fail-if-expiry<60s.

vik: one more: server can emit `X-Credential-Expiry: 60` when token is still valid but about to be deprioritized, clients can surface a warning. not necessary but helpful.

ashley: i'll draft the interface doc and a tiny proposal PR. tagging @eng-runtime for any server header ideas.

zoe: thanks! this should make onboarding for infra teams much smoother and reduce restarts. :rocket:
